summary.name: Demoscene Graphics
summary.visualIdentity: The provenance is explicit: the source requests a 1990s demoscene demo. It calls for a coherent retro graphics theme such as plasma fields, tunnels, rotating geometry, or bitmap lettering. Visual sections relate to the music and return to a shared motif.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly fits psychedelic and demoscene imagery, and listed as a good fit for the Glitch Cut transition. Inferred suitability includes intros, music-driven title sequences, event openers, credits, greetings scrollers, and retro brand messages when a supplied track exists. Unspecified: any audience or topic restriction.
summary.limitations: Do not stack plasma, tunnel, and rotozoomer effects at once, and do not switch algorithms without rhythm. Keep flashing at or below three times per second. Two-color contrast checks do not verify text over shader backgrounds, so composited frames must be rechecked. Motion references are optional and need scene-supported actions.
summary.palette: This palette is an authored suggestion, not an approved source palette. Background #171629 is the layout base, foreground #F3EACF is for text, and accents are #906ECC, #D87589, and #53ADBD. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 14.774:1, and background text on accent_2 or accent_3 measures 5.769 or 6.829:1. accent_1 at 4.469:1 is decorative only. Task-supplied colors override these, and assets must not be recolored.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion is procedural and evaluated from shared composition time, with effects changing only at scripted section boundaries. Nine optional catalog references, motion-002 through motion-040, apply only when scene assets support their defining action. Examples include the vortex passage, chapter handoff, and bitmap word cards. Interactive delivery may add pause and reduced-motion controls, but video export must not depend on live input.
summary.audio: The source does not specify audio, so no soundtrack, voice, or effect layer is fixed. Inferred suggestion: a supplied or authorized track that sets section timing, with effect changes landing on verified audio events. Narration is optional and should not compete with bitmap text. Beat synchronization must be verified by inspecting actual audio analysis first.
summary.assetRequirements: Supplied assets are unspecified. Procedural shader effects need no imported artwork, but bitmap lettering requires an approved pixel font loaded before rendering and drawn only at integer scales. Any music track must be task-provided or authorized, with precomputed event data. Reference actions that use mark geometry require inspected, approved source artwork.
summary.combinations: Demoscene Graphics works alone when one coherent shader effect and a soundtrack carry the piece. Suggested supporting style-105 provides section and beat timing for effect changes. Suggested supporting style-057 provides pixel bitmap lettering, scrollers, and greetings. Keep at most one primary effect per section, and pair only when materials and rhythm remain compatible.
summary.productionApproach: Select WebGL with GLSL and Three.js as the style renderer for procedural shaders. GLSL may also drive motion, and GSAP may own paused seekable timelines for non-shader properties, with one owner per property. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export, and Remotion is a fallback only for a documented limitation. Verify key frames, seeks, and audio sync.
